Travel could be difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will quickly increase as a strong low pressure system moves into the northern gulf. Confidence has increased on strong wind gusts around 50 to 60 mph occurring near Skagway and Haines.

* WHERE...Rock River at Moline.

* WHEN...From Monday evening to Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.2 feet, water affects 60th Street south of John
Deere Road in Moline and 56th Ave from Green Valley Park 48th St.

flood waters.

evening to a crest of 13.6 feet Tuesday evening. It will then
fall below flood stage late Thursday evening.

weather.instruction:

This helps provide higher confidence in these river forecasts. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...English River at Kalona. * WHEN...Until Tuesday evening. * IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, water has overtopped roads causing closures. This includes 130th St, Kiwi Ave, Orange Ave and Poplar Ave. Extensive agricultural land near the river is flooded. Water begins backing into town on the north side of the river. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 9:00 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 17.6 feet and slowly rising. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 18.1 feet this evening. events.title: There Is No Genocide in Gaza, and Civilian Deaths or Widespread Destruction Alone Do Not Prove Otherwise
events.description: When discussing the war in Gaza, one of the most frequent and serious allegations leveled against Israel is that it is committing genocide. Yet genocide is not simply another word for a brutal war, extensive destruction, or a tragically high civilian death toll. It is a narrowly defined crime under international law that requires very specific elements, most importantly the intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a protected group as such. Critics of Israel routinely point to civilian casualties or destruction in Gaza as though these facts alone establish genocidal intent, but they do not. This discussion will be divided into several sections: The Israel-Palestine Conflict, Palestinian Terrorist Organizations, Accusations of Stealing Land, October 7th, Intent, Rhetoric, The Genocide Convention, and Conclusion. The Israel-Palestine Conflict The Gaza war, like every war in the Israel–Palestine conflict, did not emerge from a vacuum. The pivotal starting point for the modern conflict is 1947, when the United Nations adopted Resolution 181, proposing the partition of Mandatory Palestine into independent Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem under international administration. Jewish leaders accepted partition, while Palestinian leaders and the surrounding Arab states rejected it. Rather than accept the creation of a Jewish state alongside an Arab one, Arab forces figured they outnumbered the Jews 40 million to 700,000, and they could just kill the Jews and take it all. When that failed spectacularly and resulted in what Palestinians remember as the “Nakba,” that would be the earliest starting point for the current conflict. Palestinians continued to reject generous proposals for a peaceful resolution to the conflict, most notably and most recently the Olmert Proposal in 2008. Any reasonable person could easily conclude, after reviewing these proposals and the history, that Palestinians have no evidence of any desire for peace. That is a critical factor that shapes Israeli and Jewish opinion, especially today. Palestinian Terrorist Organizations For the purpose of discussing the Gaza war, I will focus on the two most prominent terrorist organizations in Gaza, Hamas and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Both of these are terrorist organizations that consistently commit war crimes and crimes against humanity. Both of these organizations use Palestinian civilians as human shields, and both of these organizations employ the use of hostage taking to achieve political objectives. In regards to Hamas, who is the democratically elected governing body of Gaza. They have consistently embedded their military infrastructure in schools, hospitals, religious sites, historical sites, UN facilities, civilian housing, and other civilian infrastructure. They have poured billions of dollars of foreign aid into developing this terror network deeply within the civilian population. Hamas’s deliberate strategy is to ensure that they cannot be militarily targeted without massive devastation to Palestinian infrastructure and the population. Accusations of Stealing Land A frequent argument critics of Israel bring up when arguing against Israel is that Israel’s goal during war is to steal or acquire land. However, this is easily disproven given the fact that Israel has returned land for peace numerous times. Israel gave Jordan and Egypt control of Gaza and the West Bank in exchange for peace after the Arab Israeli War in 1948. Israel returned the Sinai in exchange for peace after the Six-Day War in 1982. Israel withdrew all the settlers from Gaza in 2005 in an attempt to achieve peace. Israel on many occasions has demonstrated it prioritizes peace over land acquisition. The only side that actually never offered peace was the Palestinians. October 7th On October 7th, Hamas launched a savage invasion of Israel, sending thousands of armed terrorists across the border while simultaneously firing thousands of missiles into the Jewish state. Israeli communities were overrun, civilians were murdered in cold blood and abducted, and Israel was forced into a war it did not initiate. The following day, Hezbollah opened a second front from Lebanon, beginning sustained drone and missile attacks against northern Israel in declared support of Hamas. Within hours of the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust, Israel was confronting coordinated threats from multiple fronts while fighting to defend its citizens and secure the return of its hostages. This was not just a terrorist attack, but a declaration of war by the democratically elected governing body of Gaza, Hamas. During this barbaric day, Israeli civilians were murdered in cold blood, entire communities were massacred, children were kidnapped and dragged into Gaza, and Jews were slaughtered in the largest single-day massacre of Jews since the Holocaust. ...The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Missouri...Illinois...

Mississippi River at Canton.

Mississippi River at Clarksville.

Mississippi River at Saverton.

Mississippi River at LaGrange.

Mississippi River at Hannibal.

Mississippi River at Winfield.

River forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast
precipitation for the next 24 hours.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Mississippi River at Hannibal.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening to Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, The northern end of Southside Recreation #2
Park along Bear Creek begins flooding at this height. Gate wells
are shut down to prevent the sewers from backing up.  Also at this
level pumps are set to standby.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:15 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 11.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Wednesday evening to a crest of 18.2 feet early Friday morning.
It will then fall below flood stage Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

This product, along with additional weather and stream information,
is available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx
weather.areaDesc: Pike, IL; Marion, MO

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The National Weather Service in Quad Cities has issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Iowa... Iowa River at Wapello affecting Louisa County. Iowa River at Oakville affecting Louisa County. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Iowa River at Oakville. * WHEN...From Monday morning to Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Water affects the south approach to the Iowa Highway 99 bridge near Oakville. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:00 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 9.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late tomorrow morning to a crest of 13.7 feet Wednesday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Friday morning. - Flood stage is 11.0 feet.

location.region: Louisa, IA

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued September 20 at 7:42PM CDT until September 25 at 3:00PM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Quad Cities has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Iowa...

Iowa River at Wapello affecting Louisa County.

Iowa River at Oakville affecting Louisa County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Iowa River at Oakville.

* WHEN...From Monday morning to Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Water affects the south approach to the
Iowa Highway 99 bridge near Oakville.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tomorrow morning to a crest of 13.7 feet Wednesday morning. It
will then fall below flood stage Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

The next statement will be issued by Monday evening.
weather.areaDesc: Louisa, IA

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional river and weather information is available at
www.weather.gov/lacrosse.

The next statement will be issued this evening by 930 PM CDT.

at 8:45 PM EDT Sunday was 14.4 feet.

Thursday afternoon and continue falling to 9.3 feet Friday
evening.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Florida... Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County. ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Citrus, Levy and Marion Counties. .Due to recent heavy rainfall water levels remain elevated along the Horse Creek near Arcadia. The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau. The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water levels to rise. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72. * WHEN...Until Monday evening. * IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is impassable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 12.4 feet. - Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EDT Sunday was 12.4 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 10.6 feet Wednesday evening. - Flood stage is 12.0 feet. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.4 feet on 08/30/1994. - https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Citrus, Levy and Marion
Counties.

.Due to recent heavy rainfall water levels remain elevated along the
Horse Creek near Arcadia.

The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 12.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Sunday was 12.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 10.6 feet Wednesday
evening.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.

weather.instruction:
A Flood Warning means flooding is imminent or may already be
occurring. Persons along rivers, creeks, and other waterways should
take immediate precautions to protect life and property.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Campers and hikers should be especially cautious during periods of
heavy rainfall and flooding. Know your location relative to rivers,
streams, or drainage areas. Heavy rainfall can cause quick rises on
waterways, including trails or campgrounds that are usually dry.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts 15 to 20 mph west winds across Western Yap State and Palau. Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands, occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. Both Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of JTWC's Invest 91W, (that is located near 11N144E between Yap and Guam). As 91W continues to organize showers are expected to remain widespread and heavy at times. Model guidance suggest up to 1 to 2 inches of rain a day through Wednesday, then tapering down to about 0.5 inch for the following few days. Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days. Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your local Weather Service Office.

events.title: Heat Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate hydration. * WHERE...All of Puerto Rico, including Vieques and Culebra, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. * WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 3 PM AST this afternoon. * IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; Southeast; Eastern Interior; North Central; Central Interior; Ponce and Vicinity; Northwest; Western Interior; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Southwest; Culebra; Vieques; St.Thomas...St. John.. and Adjacent Islands; St Croix

weather.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 21 at 2:00AM AST until September 21 at 3:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...All of Puerto Rico, including Vieques and Culebra, and the
U.S. Virgin Islands.


* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 3 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
weather.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Much of south-central New Mexico and Far West Texas, including El Paso, Las Cruces, and the Mesilla Valley. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos, rivers, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded, resulting in road closures. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An early season back door cold front will interact with a late season plume of deep monsoonal moisture, bringing several rounds of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday morning. - A broad swath of moderate to locally heavy rainfall is likely to affect most of the Watch area between late Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday evening, with typical, scattered monsoon season flood impacts. However, there is increasing potential for a narrow band of repeated thunderstorms which will result in particularly heavy rainfall amounts, possibly exceeding 3 inches in a 6 to 12 hour period, resulting in higher-end impacts. Forecast models currently favor placing the focus for heaviest rainfall over the Mesilla Valley and El Paso. But forecasts this far out, especially when dealing with thunderstorms, are simply not accurate enough to precisely tell yet where exactly this area of heaviest rainfall will set up. It could just as easily shift west or east and avoid the more populated corridor. - http://www.weather.gov/ElPaso

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: CORRECTED HEADLINE. ...HEAVY SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS YAP STATE AND PALAU THROUGH MIDWEEK... ...WEST WINDS TO BE GUSTY AT TIMES... An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts 15 to 20 mph west winds across Western Yap State and Palau. Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands, occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. Both Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of JTWC's Invest 91W, (that is located near 11N144E between Yap and Guam). As 91W continues to organize showers are expected to remain widespread and heavy at times. Model guidance suggest up to 1 to 2 inches of rain a day through Wednesday, then tapering down to about 0.5 inch for the following few days. Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days. Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your local Weather Service Office.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central, northeast, southeast, and west central New Mexico, including the following areas, in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio Grande Valley, Middle Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque Metro Area, San Agustin Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and Manzano Mountains including Edgewood, South Central Highlands, South Central Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, De Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands, Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and West Central Mountains. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive Tuesday and Wednesday with widespread heavy rain. Scattered occurrences of flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 2 inches in many locations along and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many locations westward to the continental divide. Stronger storms will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2 inches per hour, and storms will train repeatedly in succession over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching 4 to 6 inches over portions of central and eastern New Mexico. Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday night over eastern areas, then showers and storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return along and east of the continental divide again on Thursday. - Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas, normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams. As the event unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of storms. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
